title: Direct electroleaching and metal recovery from spent lithium-ion battery cathodes using hydroxylated solvents
content: Electroleaching using dilute HCl in hydroxylated solvents is demonstrated as an alternative to conventional acid-intensive lithium-ion battery recycling, replacing chemical reductants with an electrochemical driving force, thus minimizing reagent consumption. A systematic study across three NMC cathode chemistries, two electrode geometries (single- and double-sided), and multiple degradation states identifies applied potential and solvent composition as the main parameters controlling metal recovery. Electrode architecture emerges as a critical and underappreciated variable, with double-sided configurations presenting greater mass transport limitations for electrolyte diffusion to reach the Al current collector, triggering local acidification and boosting transition metal dissolution. Using only 0.5 M HCl at 40 °C, transition metal yields of 0.77 (in ethylene glycol) and 0.72 (in 25 vol% glycerol) are achieved from NMC83 (LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2), matching benchmarks that typically require greater acid concentrations and chemical oxidants. While anodic Al dissolution is essential to accelerate leaching, its presence requires an intermediate pH-swing precipitation prior to the selective electrodeposition of Co and Ni. This work establishes hydroxylated solvent electroleaching as an effective platform for metal recovery directly from intact spent cathodes without prior delamination or binder removal, while clarifying downstream refining requirements.
